subject: Urgent: Hosted API p95/p99 latency surge & Token/s drop — RetailPrime escalation
messages:

Cc: Procurement <contracts@retailprime.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API latency spike impacting checkout flows

Vivek —

We started seeing a dramatic increase in p95/p99 latency on the hosted API around 08:45 PT this morning. Our checkout microservice is observing timeouts and partial responses, and token/s for our streaming calls have dropped ~60% vs baseline (was ~270 token/s, down to ~110 token/s). We rolled back our local client changes and retried; issue persists.

This is blocking several production stores — revenue impact is high. Can you confirm if there's a known incident or recent deploy on your side (quantization or kernel changes)? We need an ETA for mitigation and whether you will be issuing credits for downtime.

I've attached a small error sample and a short trace. Please escalate.

Thanks,
Elaine Park
Head of Engineering, RetailPrime

We will follow up inside 30 minutes with a status update. My apologies for the disruption — we will prioritize.

Team / Elaine —

Preliminary telemetry from our ingestion pipeline: RetailPrime's requests show p95 rising from ~180ms to ~1.1s and p99 up to ~2.8s starting at 08:42 PT. Token/s for their streaming sessions show a step drop at 08:40–08:50 PT from ~260 token/s to ~100–120 token/s. Errors are predominantly 502 timeouts and some 5xx backpressure signals.

Attachments: redwood-telemetry-aggregate-20270410.csv (aggregated metrics slice).

Next steps I propose now:
1) Rishi to validate if any runtime kernel selection experiment or quantization profile rollout hit the hosted clusters during the 08:00–09:00 window.
2) If we have a deploy window match, prepare immediate rollback for the change and pin affected clusters to the prior kernel.
3) If no deploy is found, fallback to switching affected traffics to a compatible model variant (non-quantized) for RetailPrime.

I'll remain on this until resolved.

—Marissa
VP, Serving Runtime
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Elaine Park <elaine.park@retailprime.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency spike impacting checkout flows — root cause & mitigation

Short update / root cause hypothesis: after correlating deploy and kernel-selection logs, we observed a canary rollout at 08:35 PT that changed the kernel selector heuristics for the rw-opt-13B quantized family (commit a4f3b9c). The new selector favored a fused-attention kernel optimized for longer prefixes; on shorter sequences (common in RetailPrime streaming), it results in worse kernel dispatch and increases per-token latency. Combined with an aggressive quantization profile (4-bit mixed) we see reduced throughput (token/s) due to extra emulation work on certain CUDA paths.

Evidence:
- Canary rollout record: INF-DEPLOY-20270410-kerselector (08:35 PT)
- Telemetry alignment: token/s drop aligns to 08:40 PT across affected clusters.
- Error patterns: transient 502s due to request-level queuing as per autoscaler logs.

Immediate recommended mitigations (ordered):
A) Roll back the kernel-selector change for hosted clusters serving RetailPrime within the next 30 mins (fastest).
B) If rollback isn't possible for some clusters, route RetailPrime traffic to the previous model variant (rw-opt-13B-legacy-quant) or to the non-quantized rw-opt-13B-fp16 variant.
C) Short-term: increase token-concurrency limit for RetailPrime's route to avoid queue pile-up while we stabilize.

I'm starting rollback packaging now and will share the rollback plan + commands. Requesting go-ahead from Vivek for a cross-team rollback and cc'ing Laura for billing/credits messaging if this becomes prolonged.

—Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Status update: rollback of the kernel-selector change was completed at 17:10 PT on 11 Apr. Post-rollback telemetry shows RetailPrime p95/p99 back to baseline (p95 ~170ms, p99 ~420ms) and token/s restored to ~250–270 on their streaming sessions. We also temporarily increased their token-concurrency cap during remediation; that was removed at 17:30 PT.

Actions taken:
- Rishi executed coordinated rollback across 4 hosted clusters (INF-OPS runbook 7.2).
- Marissa validated traffic slices and confirmed error rates returned to normal by 17:35 PT.
- Laura: please prepare credit proposal and outreach note for RetailPrime — recommend a 10% usage credit for the impacted 6-hour window.
- Follow-up: Engineering will run a focused regression test on the kernel selector heuristics and add a canary guard that checks token/s delta for streaming workloads before promotion.

Elaine — sincere apologies for the disruption. Laura will follow up on credits and our Customer Success team will schedule a post-mortem review with your engineering leads. We will also supply a short mitigation report and proposed changes to prevent recurrence.

Vivek
CEO, Redwood Inference
